title: Playground Series - Season 6, Episode 3 Overview
why_relevant: Authoritative competition page for task definition, ROC AUC metric, submission schema, and the note that the playground data is derived from an IBM-style churn dataset.
extracted_technique: Optimize probabilistic binary classifiers for ROC AUC and treat the original telco churn dataset as an allowed public source for mapped features rather than as a blind augmentation pool.
query: Kaggle playground-series-s6e3 customer churn ROC AUC rules external data 5 submissions per day
takeaway: The competition is a binary churn problem scored by ROC AUC, and submissions must be predicted probabilities. The overview also supports using the original public telco source referenced by the synthetic playground dataset.

title: Playground Series - Season 6, Episode 3 Rules
why_relevant: Binding source for external-data allowance, submission limits, and reproducibility constraints.
extracted_technique: Use only public, reasonably accessible external data; avoid submission churn because there are five submissions per day and only two final submissions can be selected.
query: playground-series-s6e3 rules external data submission limit
takeaway: The rules explicitly allow public external data and tools, which makes the original telco churn source admissible. They also make reckless leaderboard probing a bad strategy because daily submissions are capped.

title: Categorical Data — XGBoost Documentation
why_relevant: Primary documentation for modern XGBoost categorical handling on GPU, which is central to the required XGB shortlist item.
extracted_technique: Use GPU XGBoost with `tree_method='hist'` and modern categorical support where helpful, but keep the strongest path focused on leak-safe engineered features and cross-fitted encodings.
query: XGBoost Python categorical data official docs enable_categorical hist max_cat_to_onehot
takeaway: Official docs confirm that XGBoost has a stable categorical path and the right parameter surface for GPU binary classification. In this competition, that capability is useful, but the main lift still comes from better feature design and fold-safe statistics.

title: Categorical Features — CatBoost Documentation
why_relevant: Primary documentation for CatBoost categorical handling, important because low-cardinality raw categorical columns are a natural fit here.
extracted_technique: Train CatBoost directly on raw categorical columns plus engineered numerics, using it as a complementary base learner instead of forcing all categories through the XGB encoding stack.
query: CatBoost categorical features official docs one_hot_max_size ctr
takeaway: CatBoost is a strong second family for this dataset because it handles raw categoricals natively and often blends well with XGB. It lowers preprocessing risk while still benefiting from the same external-source and arithmetic features.

title: TargetEncoder — scikit-learn Documentation
why_relevant: Primary source for safe target encoding behavior, which several high-scoring notebooks rely on heavily.
extracted_technique: Use cross-fitted target encoding for training data and plain transform for validation/test, always fit on the training fold only.
query: scikit-learn TargetEncoder official docs cross fitting fit_transform
takeaway: The sklearn docs explicitly distinguish cross-fitted `fit_transform` from plain `fit().transform()`. That distinction is critical here because target statistics are useful, but only if implemented with strict fold boundaries.

title: TabM: Advancing Tabular Deep Learning with Parameter-Efficient Ensembling
why_relevant: Broadens the search beyond Kaggle notebooks and documents a strong modern deep-tabular direction that appeared in the local competition notebook context.
extracted_technique: Keep a deep tabular diversity branch as a later-phase ablation when the tree ensemble plateaus, but avoid making it the first implementation if the dependency/runtime cost is higher than the expected marginal gain.
query: TabM arXiv October 2024 tabular deep learning
takeaway: TabM is a credible modern tabular alternative and matches the local notebook signal that deep diversity can help. For this repo, it is best treated as a phase-2 ablation unless the tree shortlist stalls.
